newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes gain, grade barrels steady late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes gain, grade barrels steady late.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices gained ground Monday, while domestic grade barrels shaded stronger on expectations for lessened competition from North Sea barrels.
July NYMEX futures closed out 10 cents higher at $20.98 a barrel, advancing on technical buying in a dull session.
July benchmark cash WTI/Cushing remained around 15 cents firmer than futures on the back of strong Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) at plus 13-15 cents, traders said.

July WTI/Cushing cash was pegged around $21.10-20 a barrel, five to seven cents stronger than NYMEX August WTI/Cushing. Off the screen, July/August rolls were minus 13 cents, seemingly accounting for the strong July EFP value.
Other talk late in the day put Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at a 15-13 cents discount to the marker, a few cents stronger than late Friday.
Sweet crudes were expected to benefit from Shell failing to fix the Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) Berge Nisa for a mid-June trans-Atlantic voyage, due to expenses.
Most grades moved in rangebound patterns, with West Texas Sour/Midland discussed late at $1.59-57 under cash WTI/Cushing, within the band seen late Friday.
"There really wasn't much to talk about in there, the grades were steady and not much moved," said a cash dealer.
Fundamentals found bearish sentiment from loaded storage capacity in the Gulf, and increased stock levels.

One trader noted that last week's American Petroleum Institute (API) data showed crude stocks running nearly 1.4 million barrels higher on the week and more than 18 million barrels ahead of same week a year earlier.
